title: Over 100 garment factories shut as wage protests turn violent
excerpt: Workers demanding a Tk 30,000 minimum wage clashed with police on 4 November. Police said more than 30 people were arrested.
content:
More than 100 garment factories in Savar and Ashulia, outside Dhaka, declared a holiday on Wednesday, 4 November, as workers protesting for a Tk 30,000 monthly minimum wage clashed with police, The Daily Star reported.

Factory authorities declared the closures from the morning because of labour unrest, Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of Ashulia Industrial Police-1, told the newspaper.

Clashes and arrests

Shamima Parveen, superintendent of police in Dhaka, said 30,000 to 40,000 workers gathered on both sides of the road near Padmar Mor in the morning and attacked police. Protesters set fire to a vehicle used by the officer-in-charge of Savar Model Police Station, who was seriously injured, according to the report.

“Yes, we used sound grenades and tear gas. The situation is better now,” she said in the afternoon. Tarikul Islam, additional superintendent of police in Dhaka, said: “We have arrested more than 30 people and are questioning them.”

Three journalists were injured at Padmar Mor in the morning, the newspaper reported. Nazmul Huda, president of the Savar Press Club, was injured around noon while broadcasting live in the same area. The crowd, arrest and injury figures come from police and have not been independently verified.

Why it matters

The unrest came on the same day the new Minimum Wage Board held its first meeting and agreed that revised wages will take effect in December. The amount is still open. Workers want Tk 30,000 a month, up from the current Tk 12,500. NGOs and labour rights groups working with garment workers in Savar and Ashulia may face disruption to field work while factories stay shut.

What to watch

Whether factories reopen on Thursday, how the wage board responds to the Tk 30,000 demand at its next meeting, and what happens to those arrested.
